Text based representation of a context tree

Source: R/ctx_tree_draw.R
draw.Rd

This function 'draws' a context tree as a text.

Usage

draw(ct, format, control = draw_control(), ...)

Arguments

ct

a context tree.

format

a character string that specifies the output format of the function. Possible values are "text" (default) and "latex". See details.

control

a list of low level control parameters of the representation. See details and draw_control().

...

additional arguments for the methods of draw().

Value

an object of class mixvlmc_draw that contains the representation of the context tree. As for other R objects, it is printed automatically when it is not assigned to a variable at top level (for instance when draw(model) is called in the console), but not inside a function or a loop where it must be printed explicitly with print(draw(model)) (see print.mixvlmc_draw()).

Details

The function uses different text based formats (plain "ascii art" and LaTeX) to represent the context tree. Fine-tuning of the representation can be done via the draw_control() function.

In addition to the structure of the context tree, draw() can represent information attached to the nodes (contexts and partial contexts). This is controlled by additional parameters depending on the type of the context tree. In general, parameters given directly to draw() specify what information is represented while details on how this representation is made can be controlled via the control parameter and the associated draw_control() function.

Format

The format parameter specifies the format used for the textual output. With the default value "text" the output is produced in "ascii art". The characters used to represent the tree are given by the charset parameter of draw_control(). By default, they are UTF-8 characters when the output supports them and ASCII characters otherwise (see the mixvlmc.charset option in mixvlmc-package).

With the "latex" value, the output is produced in LaTeX, leveraging the forest LaTeX package (see https://ctan.org/pkg/forest). Each call to draw() produces a full forest LaTeX environment. This can be included as is in a LaTeX document, provided the forest package is loaded in the preamble of the document. The LaTeX output is sanitised to avoid potential problems induced by special characters in the names of the states of the context tree.

In a knitr document (R Markdown, Quarto, ...) that produces LaTeX (e.g. a PDF output), the LaTeX representation is included as is in the document and the forest package is added automatically to its preamble (unless the document loads it, possibly with options): calling draw(model, "latex") in a chunk is enough to render the tree (see print.mixvlmc_draw()).

Examples

set.seed(0)
rdts <- sample(c(0, 1), 100, replace = TRUE)
ctree <- ctx_tree(rdts, min_size = 10, max_depth = 2)
draw(ctree)
#> ▪
#> ├─ 0
#> │  ├─ 0
#> │  └─ 1
#> └─ 1
#>    ├─ 0
#>    └─ 1
rdts_c <- sample(c("A", "B", "CD"), 100, replace = TRUE)
ctree_c <- ctx_tree(rdts_c, min_size = 10, max_depth = 2)
draw(ctree_c, control = draw_control(digits = 2))
#> ▪
#> ├─ A
#> │  ├─ B
#> │  └─ CD
#> ├─ B
#> │  ├─ A
#> │  ├─ B
#> │  └─ CD
#> └─ CD
#>    ├─ A
#>    ├─ B
#>    └─ CD
## LaTeX output
draw(ctree_c, "latex")
#> \begin{forest}
#> [\textbf{$\epsilon$}
#> [\textbf{A}
#> [\textbf{B}]
#> [\textbf{CD}]]
#> [\textbf{B}
#> [\textbf{A}]
#> [\textbf{B}]
#> [\textbf{CD}]]
#> [\textbf{CD}
#> [\textbf{A}]
#> [\textbf{B}]
#> [\textbf{CD}]]]
#> \end{forest}
